Every chapter of this book ends with a Limits layer: a list of what its scheme does not do, or does only
under conditions. This chapter gathers those lists into one place. A reader can then see in one pass where
snapy may give a wrong answer, where it is restricted, and where it is merely awkward.

Read it before you trust a configuration. If your run matches a row here, the row names the section that
explains the problem and the evidence behind it.

The chapter adds nothing of its own. Every row restates a limit that its source section already states. Where
a section and the outline disagree, the section is followed.

There are 166 items from 14 chapters. 150 are in the three tables below, which @tbl-ch16-counts counts. The
other 16 are in @sec-ch16-pending, which collects the limits of the default gravity work (the energy transfer from gravity to the flow,
booked by the corrected face form of @sec-ch06-dwork) and of the $x_1$[^rg-01fadbe6e8ea] seams: the faces where a column is cut into blocks along $x_1$, the vertical or radial direction (@sec-ch03-x1seams).[^ch16-round]

Each row has three fields. The *limit* says what the code does or does not do. The *source* names the section
that states it. The *evidence* gives what that section offers: a code location cited by symbol at the book's
pin, a registered test, an executable check with its check line, or an issue. The symbols in a row are
defined in the source section it names; this chapter does not define them again.

The evidence column cites code by its symbol at the book's pin; the line-by-line reading is in the source
section. "Stated in the section" marks a row whose section states the limit from the code without a narrower citation.

Two kinds of statement are deliberately left out. The first is the remark, made in most Limits layers, that
untested switch combinations are listed in the switch coverage matrix (@sec-ch12-matrix); that appears here as
one row rather than fourteen. The second is any statement about what an author did or did not run for a draft,
which describes the evidence of a chapter rather than a limit of the code.

Three classes are used:

- **Wrong results possible** (@sec-ch16-wrong): a configuration the code accepts can produce wrong results, or conservation that does not hold, without an error.
- **Restricted applicability** (@sec-ch16-restricted): a scheme, switch or path is limited to some configurations, or a combination is untested, so results outside them are not established.
- **Performance and usability** (@sec-ch16-usability): cost, diagnostics, documentation or defaults that surprise a user, with no effect on the results of a correct configuration.

Items where a configuration the code accepts can produce wrong results, or conservation that does not hold, without an error.

| The default float output hides relative changes below about $10^{-7}$; conservation is read from the double-precision cycle line. | @sec-ch14-netcdf | `nc_dbl` ({{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfOutput::write_output_file >}}) |
| A resumed run rewrites its last outputs, including its source restart file, and the restart index does not advance;[^ch16-277] run-to-date meters are not carried across a restart. | @sec-ch14-restart | [^ch16-277] `gravity_work_fix` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.hpp HydroImpl::gravity_work_fix >}}); the restart writer ({{< code src/output/restart.cpp RestartOutput::write_output_file >}}) |
| An output interval shorter than the step fires every step until the schedule catches up; the statistics sample accepted states only. | @sec-ch14-schedule | `MeshBlockImpl::make_outputs` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::make_outputs >}}) |
| `pd-combine` globs `*.out*.NNNNN.nc` (a five-digit stamp) in the directory, needs NCO[^rg-55084575f1eb]'s `ncrcat`, deletes its inputs unless `--no-remove` is given, and does not join per-block files. | @sec-ch14-tools | `ParseOutputFields` ({{< code python/api/pd_combine.py ParseOutputFields >}}); `CombineTimeseries` ({{< code python/api/pd_combine.py CombineTimeseries >}}) |
| The cycle line is a record, not a check: a drift in `mass0=` is visible only to a reader or a test that parses the log. | @sec-ch13-cycle | `print_cycle_info` ({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}) |
| `limcut` measures the $x_1$ flux only; a limiter acting in $x_2$ or $x_3$ shows only in `thetamin` and `thetasevere`. | @sec-ch13-limiter-meters | `_lim_cut` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}) |
| The VIC clamp meter is a run maximum: it says that a clamp bound somewhere at some time, not when or where. | @sec-ch13-vicclamp | `vicclamp` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp print_cycle_diagnostics >}}) |
| The log names redo causes but not the cells or rank that raised them; only a VIC refusal prints its column. | @sec-ch13-redo-view | `reduce_redo_flags` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reduce_redo_flags >}}) |

## Limits of the default gravity work and the $x_1$ seams {#sec-ch16-pending}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@ccf40f9565642c32be69f4b9ef0cfa6daff3f201 (chengcli/snapy, code_pin.yml)
sources: the gravity-work round recorded in [^ch16-round]; the code at the pin; the Limits
layers of the sections cited
status: draft
-->

Gravity work is the rate at which gravity does work on the flow, and snapy books it in one of several forms;
@sec-ch06 derives them. This section lists the limits of the form that is on by default, of its fixer, and of
the $x_1$ seams between blocks, including the periodic case.

The rows use the same three classes as the tables above, and cite code by symbol at the book's pin. They are
kept apart from those tables for one reason: they are read from the gravity-work round as a whole, rather than
from the Limits layer of any single section.[^ch16-round]

| limit | source | evidence |
|-------------------------------------------------------|------------------|---------------------------|
| `gravity-work`[^rg-9d4a892bae32] defaults to `face` with the corrected-PE work on (`SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT` is on by default). The conserved sum is then $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$, so for a deck that omits the key an $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ check measures the wrong invariant, and `gravity_work_defect()` stays zero because only the cell form fills it. | @sec-ch06-dwork | `gravity_work` ({{< code src/forcing/forcing.hpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::gravity_work >}}); `radial_exact_work` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::radial_exact_work >}}) |
| The cell form alone does not conserve $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$: with `gravity-work-fixer: false` its defect accumulates. The fixer is on by default only with `cell`; with $g_1\ne0$ a deck that asks for it with a face form is refused, and setup turns it off for the face forms. | @sec-ch06-cell | `gravity_work_fixer` ({{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}); ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}) |
| `face-wallc` does not conserve $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ in its two wall cells and does not get the corrected-PE work. With an implicit scheme it books the face work after the solve, and a tall column then blows up at acoustic Courant about 66.[^ch16-283] | @sec-ch06-face | `gravity_energy_correction` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}) |
| With a periodic $x_1$ boundary the corrected-PE work keeps the one-sided slope at every block edge, so a split periodic column differs from one block, and the corrected PE is not defined there ($-g_1x_1$ jumps at the periodic face). Setup only warns, once. | @sec-ch06-dwork | `TORCH_WARN_ONCE` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}); `x1_neighbors` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::x1_neighbors >}}) |
| The species covariance rows of `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE` (on by default) can export tracer that a cell does not hold, so the donor limiter runs whenever they are added, also with the positivity limiter off (`cov2` {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}; @sec-ch08-theta); `limiter: false` gives the unlimited scheme only together with `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE=0`. | @sec-ch12-flux-covariance | `_flux_covariance` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}) |
| A lone `gnomonic-equiangle` block with reflecting lateral walls loses mass under lateral flow;[^ch16-301] the single-block test of the corrected-PE work therefore uses radial flow only, and lateral flow and panel seams are tested on six panels. | @sec-ch03-gnomonic | [^ch16-301] |

: Wrong results possible in the gravity work and the $x_1$ seams. {#tbl-ch16-pending-wrong}

| limit | source | evidence |
|-------------------------------------------------------|------------------|---------------------------|
| The corrected-PE work has a form on Cartesian, spherical-polar and `gnomonic-equiangle` grids only. On any other grid the $x_1$ wall cells keep the first-order plain face work (setup warns once). When its slope stencil (the block's cells, plus the neighbour's cell at an internal $x_1$ seam) has fewer than three cells the slope term is zero, so on Cartesian and spherical-polar grids nothing is booked beyond the face form (on the cubed sphere the centroid-offset term remains). | @sec-ch06-dwork | `x1_measure` ({{< code src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp x1_measure >}}); `radial_exact_work` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::radial_exact_work >}}); `centroid_slope_stencil` ({{< code src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp centroid_slope_stencil >}}) |
| In the implicit solve the wall cells of the corrected-PE work reach order about 2, not 4:[^ch16-302] the implicit correction flux is first-order upwind and $O(\Delta t)$, its grid-scale part is $O(\Delta t\,h)$, so the wall work is second order at fixed CFL[^rg-3ca09c3904a4] and rises toward third order with $\Delta t\sim h^2$; Cartesian grids show the same. | @sec-ch06-dwork | `couple_radial_exact` ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}) |
| The fixer, which runs only with `cell` and $g_1\ne0$, refuses periodic $x_1$ boundaries, $g_2$ or $g_3\ne0$, and any step that moves mass through an $x_1$ wall face beyond round-off, so open boundaries need `gravity-work-fixer: false`. It corrects the integral, not the local second-order error of the cell work. | @sec-ch06-fixer | `gravity_work_fixer` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::gravity_work_fixer >}}); setup refusals ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}); the wall-mass check ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_gravity_work_fixer >}}) |
| A column split in $x_1$ is not bitwise equal to one block (the tests use $10^{-13}$ and $10^{-12}$). The blocks of one process in a split column must run concurrently: a block waits at most 5 minutes for the anchor of a block above it in the same process, while a remote receive has no such bound. Remote block-to-block messages allow at most 16 blocks per process. | @sec-ch03-x1seams | `take_x1_anchor` ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::take_x1_anchor >}}); `send_to_block` ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::send_to_block >}}) |
| Internal $x_1$ seam fluxes are made single-valued by averaging the two sides, across process seams only. The average masks a disagreement between the two reconstructions, and the accuracy at the seam is not analysed. | @sec-ch04-seam | `has_process_group` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}) |
| A periodic $x_1$ column has no anchor relay (each block anchors at its own top), and its block edges get neither the neighbour's density change for the corrected-PE slope nor the neighbour's face states for the covariance. | @sec-ch05-seam | `x1_neighbors` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::x1_neighbors >}}) |
| An implicit scheme needs both $x_1$ faces physical: it refuses any $x_1$ split, which a ctest arm pins, and the layout's periodic $x_1$. With a periodic boundary function on a single block the VIC closes the column as a wall, since its periodic branch is unreachable. | @sec-ch07-vic-closure | `TORCH_CHECK` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_apply_implicit_correction >}}); `Bnd` ({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}}) |

: Restricted applicability of the gravity work and the $x_1$ seams. {#tbl-ch16-pending-restricted}

| limit | source | evidence |
|-------------------------------------------------------|------------------|---------------------------|
| A deck that omits `gravity-work` gets `face` with the corrected-PE work; one that states `gravity-work: cell` gets the cell form with its fixer, reported bitwise equal to the earlier default.[^ch16-round] | @sec-ch06-conserves | `gravity_work` ({{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}) |
| The fixer's global sum depends on the decomposition at round-off, and at very large implicit steps sealed-wall round-off can exceed its bound (refusals near Courant 2500 to 2750, not universal)[^ch16-285]. | @sec-ch06-fixer | `gravity_work_fixer_sums` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}) |
| The well-balanced anchor travels down a split column block by block, so the latency of the reference grows with $n_{b1}$ (not measured). | @sec-ch05-seam | `take_x1_anchor` ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::take_x1_anchor >}}) |

: Performance and usability of the gravity work and the $x_1$ seams. {#tbl-ch16-pending-usability}

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-01fadbe6e8ea]: $x_1, x_2, x_3$ — the three coordinate directions; $x_1$ is always the vertical (radial) direction

[^rg-50e948c4d202]: nx1 — number of cells in the first coordinate direction

[^rg-ebfc2f2fc00c]: PE — potential energy

[^rg-d8c01c2e53a7]: VIC — vertically implicit correction

[^rg-17196f1aab8c]: EOS — equation of state

[^rg-d4b40b23fffb]: density-floor — minimum admissible density

[^rg-b06d1779eb4d]: limiter — whether the enclosing component enables its limiter

[^rg-a2ee54547302]: $\Delta t$ — the step

[^rg-7155fdb01b58]: coriolis — Coriolis-force options

[^rg-ff90d90bf9ab]: kappa_iso — isotropic thermal transport coefficient, interpreted according to dynamic

[^rg-db9faf126655]: $T$ — temperature [K]

[^rg-6a2dc29be3ea]: top-cool — top cooling options

[^rg-be3bec0cc3b2]: bot-heat — bottom heating options

[^rg-1d312fc939cb]: depth — number of cells over which boundary heating or cooling is distributed

[^rg-ce60eb229eae]: $E$ — total energy density, internal plus kinetic, $\rho e + \tfrac12\rho\lvert\mathbf v\rvert^2$ [J m$^{-3}$]; excludes potential energy

[^rg-5a8fdd30db1b]: MPS — Metal Performance Shaders

[^rg-e5fd6f5533b8]: vm — molar volume used by the reaction-rate model

[^rg-53322337c1b3]: nx2 — number of cells in the second coordinate direction

[^rg-f6d14d66cf07]: nx3 — number of cells in the third coordinate direction

[^rg-6d96f63d865b]: interp_order — order used for grid interpolation

[^rg-6d0d81afe25d]: nb2 — number of blocks along the second coordinate direction

[^rg-1d6fbd595d86]: WENO3 — third-order weighted essentially non-oscillatory reconstruction

[^rg-7367fe18c296]: LMARS — low-Mach approximate Riemann solver

[^rg-2e823fe9fba3]: HLLC — Harten–Lax–van Leer solver with the contact restored

[^rg-f73ac19c00f2]: $\gamma$ — mixture ratio of specific heats $c_p/c_v$, local, varies with composition, dimensionless [-]; $\gamma_{\mathrm{d}}$ is the dry value

[^rg-1dd113c26916]: non-hydrostatic — fraction of the vertical body force retained by the non-hydrostatic treatment

[^rg-3bafdb78128c]: $p$ — pressure [Pa]

[^rg-9f8b210c1766]: nghost — number of ghost cells at each boundary

[^rg-0659223b0ffa]: implicit-scheme — implicit time-integration scheme selector

[^rg-a9cb8a56905f]: YAML — YAML Ain't Markup Language, the structured input format used for decks

[^rg-cde6c69a25bc]: $\mathsf A^{\pm}$ — the Roe dissipation matrices $\mathsf R\lvert\Lambda\rvert\mathsf R^{-1}$ at faces $i\pm\tfrac12$

[^rg-af18ba914a5b]: $\mathsf I$ — the identity matrix, sized by context; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/ccf40f9565642c32be69f4b9ef0cfa6daff3f201/src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp#L349-L355)

[^rg-93beee05e98b]: $\Delta t_c$ — the time step handed to the implicit solve: $w_{2,s}\Delta t$ under rk3, $\Delta t$ otherwise

[^rg-6dc66ed3d93d]: $\mathbf W$ — primitive state vector $(\rho, v_1, v_2, v_3, p, y_1..y_{N_y})$

[^rg-4e679b29d17f]: width — physical width of the sponge layer

[^rg-16446b930188]: MPI — Message Passing Interface

[^rg-401936d2848d]: NCCL — NVIDIA Collective Communications Library; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/ccf40f9565642c32be69f4b9ef0cfa6daff3f201/external/gloo/README.md#L43-L56)

[^rg-d1be4fb0f62d]: GPU — graphics processing unit

[^rg-299481ad4048]: UCX — Unified Communication X

[^rg-5a7220aa0c8b]: CUDA — NVIDIA's parallel computing platform

[^rg-c3ec49eb0313]: API — application programming interface

[^rg-d1873d074a8e]: shock — whether reconstruction uses its shock handling

[^rg-32f5eba3262f]: type — implementation selector for the enclosing options block

[^rg-519f17b4266b]: PLM — piecewise-linear method

[^rg-81104a9e74ab]: PPM — piecewise-parabolic method

[^rg-c38c565f4c0c]: cfl — Courant-number limit for the time step

[^rg-9bb434965cbf]: SSP — strong stability preserving

[^rg-1a2efa888d13]: traditional — whether to use the traditional Coriolis approximation

[^rg-88a2b5618c6b]: omega1 — first rotation-rate component: $\Omega_z$ of the Cartesian frame under the default `type: xyz`, the $x_1$ component under `type: 123`

[^rg-3b5b90948226]: relax-bot-temp — bottom temperature-relaxation options

[^rg-a921ba73b5e8]: btemp — bottom target temperature

[^rg-8c5110e2586a]: CPU — central processing unit

[^rg-55084575f1eb]: NCO — NetCDF Operators

[^rg-9d4a892bae32]: gravity-work — form of the $x_1$ gravity work: `face` (default), `face-wallc` or `cell`

[^rg-3ca09c3904a4]: CFL — Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy
